_about.what: Centre lines of every modelled wire in mra.glb (Mini Robot Arm), measured from the CAD. Written by the wire-path study; see cad_wire_paths.md.
_about.units: millimetres, assembly space of mra.glb (Y up), as assembled
_about.conductors: Top-level keys NAUOn list the round conductors (swept tubes) found in that instance: solid = index of the connected solid inside the instance (after welding, in this study's order), radius_mm, length_mm (along the centre line), end_a / end_b = centres of the two flat end faces, points = centre line from end_a to end_b (2 mm apart or closer; closer in bends, chord error under 0.02 mm), check = distance of the tube's own vertices from that centre line (should equal the radius).
_about.chains: One entry per servo: the lead from the servo body to the plug on the shield. Distances "at_mm" are measured along the middle conductor from the servo body.
_about.across: Unit vector at the servo end pointing from the conductor that lands on the shield's G pin to the conductor that lands on the S pin (so tools/wires.py ribbon(middle, across) returns [G, V, S] = [brown, red, orange]).
_about.G_V_S: Shield digital-side columns from cad_pins.md: G at x = 50.09, V at x = 52.57, S at x = 55.06.
_about.passes: chains[servo].passes: every slot or hole in the wood that the lead goes through, in order. at_mm = distance along the middle conductor from the servo body to where it crosses the middle of the plate thickness; in_thickness_from/to_mm = the stretch whose tube is inside the plate thickness; conductors_at_mid_plane.tube_to_edge_mm = gap between that conductor and the nearest cut edge; feature_outline = the cut edge as 3D points at mid-thickness (the cut goes straight through the 3 mm).
_about.comes_near: chains[servo].comes_near: every wood part (and the shield) whose surface comes within 2 mm of the lead, with the closest gap between the tube surface and the part.
_about.plug_position: plug_position = centre of the plug face that goes onto the header pins, as seated; plug_direction = the way the plug moves to seat (pins point the opposite way); plug_cable_end = centre of the opposite face, where the conductors enter.
